legend.yes: The policy language can express a trust-robust detection natively.
legend.partial: Expressible with effort, custom helpers, or external correlation.
legend.no: Not expressible in the stock policy language; requires sensor changes.

TB-01 privilege re-validation at event t.evidence: Tetragon supports kprobes on capset/commit_creds and credential-change events; Tracee exposes credential/signature events; Falco can read cap_effective but its rule language has no native event-time capability-change state machine.

TB-02 immutable workload identity allowl.evidence: All three support image/namespace/label filters, but none binds an allowlist to signed digest plus service account by default; wildcards remain permitted.

TB-03 fail-closed on telemetry gaps.evidence: Falco offers proc_name_exists; Tetragon documents dropped-event metrics; Tracee documents container=new race limitations. None treats a missing field as an alertable condition by default.

TB-04 semantic (non-name-based) matching.evidence: All three can filter on syscall type, path and kernel object; shipped examples nevertheless frequently use binary names.

TB-05 LSM cross-check for argument integ.evidence: Tetragon supports lsmhooks (e.g. bprm_check_security) and Tracee exposes LSM-based signature events; Falco's default ruleset is predominantly syscall-event based.

TB-06 time-series identity / credential.evidence: Tetragon and Tracee both document post-exec credential-change visibility; Falco's shipped rules rely on exec-time snapshots and launch metadata.
